$comment: Salted SHA-256 digests of names that must never appear in this public repository.
WHY HASHES AND NOT THE LITERALS: a guard that stores the forbidden string reintroduces
the exact exposure it exists to prevent. Anyone grepping this repo for the name would
find it here. So the guard stores digests and hashes candidate tokens to compare.
WHAT THIS IS NOT: the salt is committed beside the digests, and the inputs are short
dictionary-ish words, so this is NOT cryptographically secret — a determined party with
this file can brute-force the inputs. That is accepted and deliberate. The property being
bought is that the name does not appear in PLAINTEXT in a public tree and cannot be
reintroduced by accident, grep, search-engine index or model training scrape. It is a
hygiene ratchet, not a secret store. Do not use this mechanism for credentials.
TO ADD AN ENTRY you need the literal, which is deliberately not written down here:
and append the digest with a `why` that does not name the thing.
Enforced by scripts/check-forbidden-names.mjs, run in the `Authz / open-core guards` job.

entries.why: A third-party company name, unrelated to Alethia Labs. It was used as a test-fixture org slug. Publishing it associates an unaffiliated firm with this project's code and can create obligations Alethia Labs never agreed to. Removed in the tree 2026-09-22; it remains in git history by a recorded decision.

The e2e GCP project id, which embeds the same third-party name. GCP project ids are IMMUTABLE, so this cannot be fixed by renaming the project — docs and runbooks refer to it as ${GCP_E2E_PROJECT_ID} instead, and the literal lives only in repo variables. Removed in the tree 2026-09-22.
